whatItIs.text: A ribbed-stalk vegetable from the parsley family, eaten raw, cooked, or juiced; its seeds double as a spice and the base of celery salt.

historyNote.text: Celery has been used as a vegetable since ancient times — Greek writers describe its cultivation and Egyptians put it in funeral garlands; the word goes back to Mycenaean Greek, written in Linear B. It was long prized as a cleansing winter vegetable against salt-meat diets.

howToChoose.text: Choose crisp stalks with fresh leaves and no brown or slimy patches at the base; the strings should snap rather than bend.

storage.text: Refrigerate wrapped so it does not lose moisture and crunch.

useItUp.text: Limp celery perks up in iced water for salads, or goes straight into stock, soup bases, and braises where crispness does not matter. The leaves are the most flavourful part.

substitutions.note: same crunch with an anise note; use less if the dish is delicate
